request.current_synthesis: Observed in M2: the compiled model uses 0.02 s control intervals, 5.0 joint torque at unit control, approximately 0.0102-0.0119 joint mass-matrix diagonal terms across the tested radii, and approximately 421-491 rad/s^2 initial unit-control acceleration. A 25-control-step saturated step reached roughly 9.2-10.0 rad/s joint speed and the post-release joint velocity fell below 0.02 rad/s by control step 30-34. A one-control-step saturated impulse produced up to about 0.040 m end-effector displacement at the outer radius, versus about 0.012 m at the inner radius. Interpretation: gross actuator authority and damping are not the leading hard ceiling for reaching or settling; the plant can become highly sensitive to poorly regulated 20 ms action changes, especially near the outer radius. Competing explanations now are (A) policy/distribution limitation, with failures concentrated in the untrained inner annulus or inconsistent IK branch use, versus (B) learned closed-loop precision limitation, with entry velocity or residual oscillation causing hold interruptions despite adequate plant authority. M2 does not measure a learned policy, action saturation during task behavior, branch consistency, or continuous hold semantics, so it cannot establish which explanation dominates.

If failures correlate with action saturation and residual velocity, prioritize control-aware policy design; if failures correlate with radius and branch while stable holds occur when reached, prioritize training coverage and branch-consistent representation.
